Jieznas Jewish Cemetery

Jewish Cemetery · Kauno apskritis, Lithuania

Demolished. Jieznas's Jewish community, settled from the first half of the 19th century, had no cemetery of its own until 1912, using instead the cemetery of nearby Butrimonys, documented elsewhere in this collection, where 1,400 people were killed in a single 1941 action. About 300 Jews lived in Jieznas by the 1940 Soviet occupation; Lithuanian nationalists began attacking the town's Jews even before German forces arrived in 1941, and by September almost all had been murdered — only 18 escaped, and just 4 survived the war.
